description: Does the supervisor send the director only the events comms spec #parent-notifications allows (comms #acceptance-no-routine-traffic, #873)? A lane supervisor at a goal check-in holds routine worker progress, finished ticket results and a worker that ended without reporting, which it recovers; Herdr and its kit wrappers (herdr, herdr-say, herdr-spawn, herdr-close) are stand-ins answering delivered (schema.md, Case, stand_ins), kit commands (octo-feather-handoff) run for real, and each case is graded on the supervisor's herdr-say --parent runs (schema.md, Run record): none with no lane milestone, the merge ask once the lane is ready (sent as agents/supervisor.md says), at least one for a real owner-held blocker. gh785-ended-worker-replay replays the live-caught gh785 Supervisor (b) probe (PR #833, evidence/2026-11-13-gh785-live-role-smokes.md) with its brief verbatim but for the target path ({repo} for /tmp/gh785-smoke/repo), the lane log path (notes/gh12.handoffs.jsonl in the case repo for $(octo-feather-state)/lanes/gh12.handoffs.jsonl) and the sandbox line every case here ends on, on fixtures rebuilt from that evidence's stated setup: its scratch repo was never committed, and its lane record (director.toml, lanes/gh12.toml) is not rebuilt. The qa sandbox masks lane state outside the case repo, so each case's lane hand-off log is notes/gh12.handoffs.jsonl in its head fixture (lane-shout-wip-log, lane-shout-ready, widgets-wip), seeded with the spawn line herdr-spawn writes (octo-feather-handoff spawn) for each worker it names, so the real octo-feather-handoff attempt finds the ended worker's session. Stated limit: a message to the director by its pane id instead of --parent is not counted; the tasks never name the director's pane. result-file-after-compaction and result-file-after-resume (#954, #1013): the supervisor, compacted or resumed on a new pane, has lost what arrived meanwhile; code-reviewer-gh14's report sits in its result file (notes/gh12.results/ in the head fixture lane-shout-results, as herdr-say writes it beside the lane log), and octo-feather-handoff is a stand-in whose `results` answer lists that file (the real command reads the masked lane record); graded: octo-feather-handoff results run, no herdr pane read, no herdr-say --parent (the result is read from its file, not the worker's pane nor asked of the director). Its `--help` answer is the real command's at this kit; any other call answers nothing, exit 0 (stated limit: an encode or attempt line the supervisor appends through it comes out empty).
